A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same NINT research, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Existing content can be matched reliably, including material shifted by pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original image, audio, and 3D shape fitting experiments and ablations in Sections 4 and 6–8, including Tables 1–8.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original super-resolution, FFHQ image fitting, and NTK timing results in Sections 9–11.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and the hybrid sampling schedule retain the same scoring and training procedure. Section 11 newly explains computing the existing NTK-gradient product using VJP/JVP operations; it does not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: v2 adds DIV2K super-resolution, requiring reconstruction at coordinates beyond the low-resolution training input, and 1024×1024 FFHQ image fitting. These extend task and data-population coverage beyond the retained Kodak/DIV2K fitting, LibriSpeech audio, and Stanford 3D shape experiments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding original experiments, including EVOS variants and Expansive Supervision settings. The new experiments use existing comparators Stand., INT, and EVOS; no new comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: Section 9 adds a protocol that downsamples 512×512 images to 256×256, trains on the low-resolution input, and evaluates high-resolution reconstruction at 1,000 iterations and time to 20 dB. Section 10 evaluates FFHQ at 1,000 iterations and time to 30 dB. Previously reported evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 11 adds a focused overhead analysis addressing the cost of NTK scoring: 3.2 ms, or 3.6% of total selection, for a specified Kodak/SIREN/GPU configuration. Existing network-size, architecture, hyperparameter, and sampling ablations in Tables 3–5 and 8 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results and timing measurements remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 remain numerically unchanged, while Tables 9–10 and Figures 9–10 add results for previously unevaluated settings. For super-resolution, NINT reaches 20 dB in 7.91 s versus Stand.'s 8.63 s, but has lower 1,000-iteration PSNR: 24.266 versus 24.390. On FFHQ, time to 30 dB is 97.32 versus 141.53 s. Section 11 adds scoring-cost measurements, and Section 7.2 corrects the Unif. CHD example to 5.958×10^-3, matching the unchanged Table 7.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Equations 1–8, and training-dynamics assumptions are retained. Section 11's identity J(Jᵀg)=Kg explains evaluation of the existing NTK product without adding a substantive theoretical result, proof, or assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about NTK-guided selection, approximately halved training time, reconstruction quality, and adaptability. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets super-resolution as recovering missing high-frequency information, the FFHQ experiment as supporting transfer of the NTK mechanism across scales, and the timing measurement as demonstrating negligible overhead. Section 9 also overstates quality superiority over Stand.: Table 9 favors Stand. on all three quality metrics at 1,000 iterations.

D1.justification: Section 11 newly discloses matrix-free computation through a VJP followed by a JVP, together with the model, image resolution, and hardware used for profiling. v2 also adds a project-page link. These clarify implementation and access information; retained experiments' implementation settings otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Nonparametric Teaching for Attention Learners, listed as reference 77 in v2, to the nonparametric teaching context. The remaining research positioning is retained; shifted reference numbers do not represent additional works or baselines.

P1.justification: v2 appends Sections 9–11, adds acknowledgments and a corresponding-author designation, and makes a small numerical prose correction. The existing narrative, terminology, and section sequence are otherwise substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 9–10 and Figures 9–10 while retaining Tables 1–8 and Figures 1–8. Figure 2 and Algorithm 1 are rearranged within page 4, with additional spacing and pagination changes but no extensive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Section 11 improves practical assessability by explaining matrix-free NTK computation and measuring its overhead; the super-resolution and FFHQ experiments broaden empirical support. These gains are tempered by Section 9's overstated quality claim: Table 9 favors Stand. on all three fixed-iteration quality metrics, although NINT reaches the target faster. The net improvement is useful but limited.
